newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Chechen leadership reported falling out over poll.
newsitem.headline: Chechen leadership reported falling out over poll.

text.p: Divisions in Chechnya's separatist leadership hardened on Thursday when the president fired a minister and other government officials quit ahead of elections in the breakaway region, Russian news agencies said.

Interfax and Itar-Tass news agencies quoted sources in the leadership as saying president Zelimkhan Yandarbiyev had sacked Ruslan Kutayev, a minister in the region's provisional secessionist government who was responsible for relations with Russia.
Several other leading separatist figures, interviewed by Reuters, were unable to confirm the reports immediately.

The agencies said Yandarbiyev accused Kutayev of too actively supporting the election campaign of Aslan Maskhadov, the commander of the separatist army, in his bid to wrest the presidency from Yandarbiyev in a vote scheduled for January 27.
Interfax said Yandarbiyev, who was appointed last April after the death in a rocket attack of Dzhokhar Dudayev, had also sacked all advisers to Maskhadov, who is favourite to win.
Maskhadov has already formally resigned as government leader in order to campaign.
Tass quoted a spokesman for Kutayev's Chechen National Independence Party as saying all the party's members had quit their government positions in protest at their leader's sacking.
They included five ministers in the coalition government set up after the rebels recaptured the capital Grozny from Russian troops in August and signed a peace deal with Moscow.
Five first deputy ministers and 10 deputy ministers also resigned, Tass said.

In another sign of increasing tension in the leadership, five of whose best-known figures are contesting the presidential election along with 11 other candidates, guerrilla field commander Shamil Basayev lashed out at his rivals on Thursday.
Tass quoted Basayev as sharply criticising Yandarbiyev and former government spokesman Movladi Udugov, accusing him and Kutayev of propagating a variant of Islam alien to Chechnya.
Udugov, Yandarbiyev, Basayev, Maskhadov and former guerrilla commander Akhmed Zakayev are seen as the five main candidates in the race for the presidency, which has the blessing of Moscow.
However, all favour full independence for the mainly Moslem region of one million on Russia's southern frontier, something Russia is not prepared to contemplate.
Russia Foreign Minister Yevegeny Primakov warned on Thursday that Chechnya could soon break away from Russia unless Moscow moved quickly to block the process.
"There is a real threat that Chechnya could split from Russia," news agencies quoted Primakov as telling the cabinet.
The major task for the Russian government and other bodies is "to think about it now and not let this happen", RIA quoted him as saying.

Interfax quoted Primakov as saying the Russian government could help prevent a split by streamlining relations with the states of the Organisation of the Islamic Conference and the Chechen diaspora in various regions of Russia and overseas.
Moscow said on Sunday it had withdrawn all the troops it sent to Chechnya two years ago to stop it splitting from Russia. Tens of thousands of people, mainly civilians, died in the war.

But it is sticking by its insistence that Chechnya must remain part of Russia, both to stop other ethnic groups from pressing for autonomy and to keep a grip on the lucrative oil pipeline which runs through the turbulent North Caucasus region.
